traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria for story 010.3-DEV-MIGRATE-TO-SUPPORTS are implemented and verified:
- Optional Warning & Configurable Enforcement: The `prefer-implements-annotation` rule exists, is of type `suggestion`, and is **not** included in recommended/strict presets by default (configs built from TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES omit it). Tests explicitly assert it is disabled in both presets and demonstrate configuring severities `off`, `warn`, and `error`. This matches REQ-OPTIONAL-WARNING and REQ-CONFIG-SEVERITY.
- Auto-fix Support & Single Story Conversion: The rule’s meta declares `fixable: "code"`; helper functions `collectStoryAndReqMetadata`, `buildImplementsAutoFix`, and `applyImplementsReplacement` implement a conservative auto-fix that: - Only acts when there is a single story path and at least one simple `@req` line. - Collapses multiple `@req` lines into a single `@supports` line enumerating all REQ IDs. Tests verify both the single @req case and the multi-@req single-story case with exact expected output, satisfying REQ-AUTO-FIX and REQ-SINGLE-STORY-FIX.
- Multi-story Detection & Mixed Usage Handling: The rule detects and reports: - Mixed @story/@req with existing @supports lines using the `cannotAutoFix` message with a descriptive `reason` value. - Multiple distinct @story paths in the same block using the `multiStoryDetected` message. Both behaviors are explicitly tested. This fulfills REQ-MULTI-STORY-DETECT.
- Preserve Order & Format: The auto-fix code replaces only the @story line with the @supports line and removes @req lines while preserving all other comment lines and using the original indentation and `*` prefix from the @story line. That preserves JSDoc structure and annotation ordering within the comment (the @supports line occupies the original @story line position). This matches REQ-PRESERVE-FORMAT.
- Both Formats Valid & Backward Compatibility: When the rule is disabled (the default) it has no effect. Even when enabled, tests confirm it intentionally ignores comments containing only @story, only @req, or only @supports, and those with @story + @supports but no @req or @req + @supports but no @story. Existing validation rules for @story/@req/@supports remain unchanged and are thoroughly tested elsewhere. This satisfies REQ-BACKWARD-COMPAT-VALIDATION and the “Both Formats Valid” acceptance criterion.
- Valid Output: Auto-fix is deliberately limited to simple patterns; complex @story or @req lines null out the storyPath and so disable the fix, while still emitting a recommendation. The resulting @supports annotations are of the same syntactic form already validated by the `valid-annotation-format` tests. This covers REQ-VALID-OUTPUT and the Quality Standards acceptance criterion.
- Documentation: There is a dedicated rule doc (docs/rules/prefer-implements-annotation.md) and a user migration guide (user-docs/migration-guide.md) describing this rule, its optional nature, configuration, and auto-fix behavior, including concrete before/after examples. This meets the Documentation acceptance criterion.
Given the implemented rule, configuration defaults, comprehensive unit tests tied to this story, passing test suite, and supporting documentation, the specification in docs/stories/010.3-DEV-MIGRATE-TO-SUPPORTS.story.md is fully implemented and verified.
